Industry News: Bitcoin’s blockchain keeps growing as its live ledger sheds 25 million entries

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, bitcoin’s set of unspent transaction outputs fell to about 164.1 million on Nov.
  • Industry observers note that blockchain.com’s unspent-output series last recorded 164,079,624 outputs on Nov.
  • Each point is the last Blockchain.com reading of the UTC day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bitcoin’s set of unspent transaction outputs fell to about 164.1 million on Nov. 22, roughly 25 million fewer entries than on Dec. 22, 2024. The network was still confirming hundreds of thousands of transactions a day. A single transaction can spend several existing outputs or create several fresh ones, so a busy day can leave Bitcoin’s live ledger with fewer entries.

Industry observers note that blockchain.com’s unspent-output series last recorded 164,079,624 outputs on Nov. 22, down 13.2% from the last Dec. 22, 2024 reading of 189,085,860. Firsthand Bitcoin’s published comparison used 164,088,181 for Nov. 22 and 189,282,514 for its December 2024 series high. That pair implies a drop of 25.2 million, and Firsthand placed the November reading at its lowest since Feb. 20, 2024.

Each point is the last Blockchain.com reading of the UTC day. The count excludes OP_RETURN outputs. The source export has no reading for Nov. 15, 2025.

Source: Blockchain.com Unspent Transaction Outputs.

According to recent reports, the daily transaction series recorded 638,018 confirmed transactions on Nov. 21 and 716,530 on Nov. 22. Across the seven days through Nov. 22, Bitcoin averaged about 669,000 confirmed transactions a day.

It has been revealed that an unspent transaction output, or UTXO, is a portion of bitcoin that a previous transaction made available to spend under specific conditions. When a full node checks a newly introduced transaction, it looks up the earlier outputs that the transaction inputs reference. If the transaction spends five existing outputs and creates one spendable output, the set loses four entries. It still counts as one confirmed transaction.

An example of how one confirmed Bitcoin transaction can shrink the set of outputs that nodes track.

A transaction adds one to the daily tally while changing the live set by the net number of outputs it creates and spends.

Industry observers note that the example uses hypothetical outputs. The network-wide figures measure the net result across all transactions.

Recent findings suggest that illustrative ordinary transaction with five distinct unspent outputs consumed by its inputs and one new spendable output created. The net change is one minus five, or minus four outputs. Each marker represents one output without encoding its BTC value.

Recent findings suggest that the example uses hypothetical outputs. The network-wide figures measure the net result across all transactions.

Miners collected an average of 2.84 BTC a day in transaction fees in the 30 days through Nov. 21. That is a network-wide fee total expressed as a daily average. The cost of combining small outputs in a single transaction depends on the fee rate and the size of that transaction. Each additional input generally adds size, so lower fee rates make the same consolidation cheaper. The aggregate counts leave open how much consolidation contributed to the decline.

In a recent development, BTC.network’s supply audit counted 162,917,807 outputs in a copy of the set taken by its own node at block 976,975 on Nov. 22. Blockchain.com’s series counts valid outputs and excludes OP_RETURN outputs, which can carry data without creating a spendable entry. An exact comparison would require a shared block reference and comparable counting methods.

Sources indicate that A smaller set leaves full nodes with fewer spendable entries to track. Bitcoin Core’s documentation lists the number of outputs and estimated chainstate disk usage as separate measurements. Disk usage, the size of the historical blockchain, the amount of bitcoin those entries represent, and the number of wallets each require their own measure.

#144430. Latest Update: China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

Latest Update: China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong.
  • In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight.
  • The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC states every system worked normally.

In a recent development, it wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

Sources indicate that the CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

In a recent development, the program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL released its aviation unit.

According to recent reports, CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

Industry observers note that COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, Latest York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

Industry observers note that heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

Recent findings suggest that for years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

In a recent development, look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

According to recent reports, and this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

Industry observers note that china also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

In a recent development, if you’re following the electrification of transport, the cheapest place to start is your own roof: home solar can power your EV for close to nothing. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.
  • Sources indicate that chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet.
  • “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

Sources indicate that chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

“High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the manufacturer won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the substantial bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

“Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

While specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the organization has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

Those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The significant trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

SOURCE | IMAGES: Eacon; via The Driven.

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bitcoinmagazine

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.
  • Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500.
  • Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.

Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory.

Sources indicate that chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported.

Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600.

Sources indicate that bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record.

Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff.

Recent findings suggest that coinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said.

In a recent development, the dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.

Strategy (MSTR) fell about 8.4% to near $78.90, adding to the losses after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 5.5% to near $103. Robinhood (HOOD) lost about 9.6% and Circle (CRCL) fell about 7.9%.

According to recent reports, bitcoin miners fared worst. MARA Holdings (MARA) sank about 17% to near $5.17, IREN (IREN) fell about 17% and CleanSpark (CLSK) dropped about 16%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 8.4%, and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell about 9.4%. Many miners have expanded into AI data centers, tying their shares to the chip selloff.

The bitcoin price is now down more than 50% from its record above $126,000, set in October 2025.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $58,300.

Adventurous baby black bear wins 2026 Courageous Cub Award

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (417 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, one little bear cub in Southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest is a true model of bravery.
  • According to recent reports, “This little cub of Dory’s went on a massive adventure.
  • Black bears like this family have a very keen sense of smell.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, one little bear cub in Southeastern Alaska’s Tongass National Forest is a true model of bravery. The park’s rangers have awarded the unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) cub with the 2026 Courageous Cub award for persevering when he got himself in a little pickle this summer. The cub belongs to a forgetful mother bear named Dory, who had two cubs this season.

According to recent reports, “This little cub of Dory’s went on a massive adventure. He got lost, ran down the trail a half mile and approached visitors as if to ask, ‘Are you my mommy?’ Then got scared and ran off in the wrong direction,” the Tongass rangers write. “Hours later he came running back up the trail sniffing out where mama was.”.

Black bears like this family have a very keen sense of smell. It is debated just how far away they can smell, but it is at least two miles and could be up to 20. Fortunately, the cub was able to use some of that sniffing power to find both Dory and his other sibling.

The rangers at Tongass National Forest are currently awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States. It covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau, and includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. This makes the creek a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, at least 39 bears feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Hits $63K on Nvidia News—Could It Be a Trap?

Risk appetite returned in force on Monday—but massive players aren’t acting like the bottom is in.

Bitcoin price climbed approximately 4% to around $63,200 on November 23, staging a sharp recovery after plunging to a Saturday low of $55,081 over the weekend.

The rebound followed a sudden turnaround in U.S. tech equities and a wave of forced liquidations across crypto derivatives markets.

US markets staged a sharp rebound on Monday, November 23, led by a stunning 26% surge in Nvidia (NVDA) shares, after the manufacturer’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.Read the release: https://t.co/x4bnjiSVil.

The move helped reverse the recent tech and AI sell-off, sending Nasdaq 100 futures up 3.1% and S&P 500 futures up 2.4%, lifting risk appetite across global markets, including crypto.

Sources indicate that bitcoin price recovery was further amplified by a short squeeze. More than $440 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $370.2 million in shorts. Bitcoin short liquidations alone accounted for $172.91 million, according to CoinGlass.

Sources indicate that despite Monday’s bounce, underlying institutional data reveals ongoing caution. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $669.16 million in net outflows on Friday—their largest single-day capital exit since June 25, according to SoSoValue.

Over the past week, spot Bitcoin ETFs lost roughly $1.8 billion, marking their fourth consecutive week of net outflows.

Industry observers note that corporate accumulation also showed signs of restraint. Strategy (MSTR), the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, purchased 457 BTC for $28 million last week—a modest addition compared to the $212 million it spent repurchasing its own STRC stock over the same period.

“The biggest Bitcoin corporate holder isn’t capitalizing on the dip,” crypto investor Ted Pillows noted on X.

Market analysts remain divided on whether the weekend drop marked a final floor or a temporary pause before another leg down.

Prominent trader Astronomer (@Astronomer_zero) suggested on X that while Bitcoin approached a macro bottom near the $56,000 level over the weekend, the current move to $63,200 is likely a relief bounce rather than a confirmed bottom, warning that a downward retrace remains probable.

$btc 56k bottom looking really good now, with a 10%+ bounce so far.Even though I think this will retrace and I deem it just a bounce, it is a very crucial bounce and a strong bounce like this has significance and is exactly what we wanted to see.If you remember my short… https://t.co/TzN9MxF9tc pic.twitter.com/WitozYCG5Z.

However, the trader argues that a durable bottom is forming soon and expects Bitcoin to hold above $50,000.

His thesis centers on Bitcoin’s estimated electricity production cost—at the moment around $60,300—which has historically served as a reliable long-term accumulation zone during cycles in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2026.

When prices dip below mining electricity costs, inefficient miners shut down, network difficulty adjusts downward, and supply pressure eases, establishing a technical and economic floor near $50,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie unveiled the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the tech giant really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

It has been revealed that “We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” says Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

According to recent reports, greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” remarked Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of major battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The firm notes the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

Meet SHRINCS: Bitcoin's Emerging Frontrunner for a Post-Quantum Signature

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.
  • “We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP).
  • Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blockstream Research Director Jonas Nick, with Mikhail Kudinov and collaborators, published a security analysis on Thursday for SHRINCS, advancing an emerging frontrunner for a post-quantum signature scheme in Bitcoin.

“We need all the possible feedback—engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said in reference to a draft of SHRINCS’ Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP). “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.".

Notably, SHRINCS is a hash-based signature scheme that leverages SHA-256 to anchor its security in battle-tested primitives that are already used by Bitcoin, representing a conservative effort to minimize the proposal’s trust assumptions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

That noted, the scheme comes with trade-offs, most notably by introducing potential security vulnerabilities at the implementation level if misused. The scheme combines two spending paths: a small, more efficient stateful signature option and a larger, more costly stateless path with fewer security risks on the implementation side.

Although stateful signatures are compact, preserving Bitcoin’s ability to process transactions efficiently, a user can trigger a critical failure—where an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal funds if a one-time state is accidentally reused. Because SHRINCS’ stateful path relies on one-time keys that can only safely sign a single transaction, wallet developers must carefully track each key’s state.

According to recent reports, “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” Nick told Head of MARA Foundation Isabel Foxen Duke during a recent appearance on MARA Foundation TV. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”.

According to Nick, for SHRINCS to work safely in the real world, its specification and corresponding wallet implementations must automatically enforce the stateless path fallback in any situation where a state counter could possibly be compromised.

While some customers might gravitate toward stateless signatures out of caution, Nick warns that widespread adoption could bloat the blockchain and drive up fees across the network.

Bitcoin’s current ECDSA signatures are typically 71 bytes long (and Taproot Schnorr signatures are 64 bytes). Under SHRINCS, stateful signatures are anywhere from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while stateless ones are 5,777 bytes. That mentioned, optimizations of both signature paths have been accelerating with the support of AI-based research, Nick noted.

“We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very massive signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”.

As the SHRINCS working group—which includes researchers backed by nonprofits including Brink and OpenSats—continues to refine the proposal’s specification, Blockstream researchers stress that getting the cryptographic foundation right is only half the battle.

Whether the broader Bitcoin ecosystem is ready to embrace SHRINCS’ inherent trade-offs will depend heavily on feedback from the network’s stakeholders in the months ahead. Meanwhile, Nick and Kudinov are requesting review of the proposal and the security analysis.

André Beganski is a Senior Content Manager at MARA Foundation, producing content on topics including the intersection of quantum computing and cryptography. He has previously worked for Decrypt.

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (671 w)

Tech Report: Divers release first footage of SS ‘United States’ after intentional sinking

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It took a few hours longer than expected, but the SS United States now rests at the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico.
  • Ahead of the next phase in the United States’ recycled life, divers from the RV Explorer swam to document the vessel’s location and post-scuttling condition.
  • Recent findings suggest that “It was just epic,” diver Rustin Cassway told a local Philadelphia news outlet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took a few hours longer than expected, but the SS United States now rests at the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico. The nearly 1,000-foot-long ocean liner sank off the coast of Pensacola, Florida, to a depth of about 190 feet on November 11, where it is now officially the world’s largest artificial reef. In the years ahead, biologists and conservationists will monitor the vessel’s remains as numerous marine species slowly convert the ship into their own home.

Ahead of the next phase in the United States’ recycled life, divers from the RV Explorer swam to document the vessel’s location and post-scuttling condition. On November 13, the team released a brief video of their successful excursion. Interestingly, the footage shows the ship is resting upright on the ocean floor despite initially sinking on its side.

Recent findings suggest that “It was just epic,” diver Rustin Cassway told a local Philadelphia news outlet. “It was very cleaned up. I mean, you could see people really took their time to clean it really nicely.”.

Recent findings suggest that the project marks the first time ecologists will be able to monitor a shipwreck’s transformation in real-time. Researchers now proposal to conduct annual visits to the SS United States to chart not only the artificial reef’s progress, but how the ship’s materials may affect the surrounding ocean conditions.

Industry observers note that in its heyday, the SS United States was the world’s fastest ocean liner. Larger than the RMS Titanic, she was the most powerful, advanced, and modern passenger liner when she first took to the ocean in 1952. In addition to the 1,700 passengers, 7,935 quarts of ice cream and 500 pounds of caviar were also on board. During that maiden voyage (July 3-7, 1952), she broke the transatlantic speed record held by the RMS Queen Mary by over 10 hours. The United States made the crossing from the United Kingdom to Newly introduced York in three days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes at an average speed of 40.96 mph.

She was designed by naval architect William Francis Gibbs (August 24, 1886 – September 6, 1967), and was built to be converted into a troopship if the United States Navy needed during a time of war. But she never was called into military service. Instead, the United States transported immigrants and celebrities, including future President and First Lady John and Jacqueline Kennedy, actors Grace Kelly, Gary Cooper, and Marilyn Monroe, artist Salvador Dali, and musicians Duke Ellington and Irving Berlin. Walt Disney even filmed parts of the 1962 comedy Bon Voyage aboard the ship.

An engineering marvel, some of the key design features were in the rudder, radar mast, and propellers.

Sources indicate that the rudder was designed for good maneuverability at high speeds. The Titanic’s relatively small rudder was one factor behind the ship’s collision with an iceberg and tragic sinking in 1912.

The SS United States had the latest radar equipment, which allowed the crew to see the locations of  other ships and objects in the ocean despite the weather. It was among the first ocean liners to use radar, which was located at one of the highest points on the ship, so in addition to her radar “eyes,” a lookout could be stationed there to warn the captain of any danger in the ship’s path.

In a recent development, considered a top-secret design, the ship had four propellers—two with four blades and two with five. According to the SS United States Conservancy, this configuration was tested and selected for its superior hydrodynamic performance. The propeller design was overseen by a pioneering Gibbs & Cox engineer named Elaine Kaplan.

It has been revealed that ocean liners became a less attractive option once air travel became quicker and less expensive. The SS United States ceased operations in 1969, and stayed in drydock in several cities before becoming the world’s largest artificial reef.

Tech Report: Robo-frog swims with liquid crystal muscles powered by light

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (457 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A silicone frog built by engineers at Denmark’s Aarhus University can’t swim nearly as fast as its amphibian inspiration, but it still manages to get the job done without any moving parts.
  • The team’s novel system is detailed in a study recently published in the journal Advanced Materials Technologies.
  • According to recent reports, “I could easily imagine these robots being used as toys before we see them on rescue missions,” Cecilie Ryberg, Aarhus University chemist and study co-author, mentioned in a profile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A silicone frog built by engineers at Denmark’s Aarhus University can’t swim nearly as fast as its amphibian inspiration, but it still manages to get the job done without any moving parts. The odd invention owes its slow-but-steady aquatic maneuvering to a set of six artificial muscles specially designed to contract when exposed to near-infrared light.

The team’s novel system is detailed in a study recently published in the journal Advanced Materials Technologies. Although similar setups may one day boost the capabilities of soft robots tasked with search and rescue or environmental monitoring, its creators are a bit more realistic about this frog-bot’s near-term uses.

According to recent reports, “I could easily imagine these robots being used as toys before we see them on rescue missions,” Cecilie Ryberg, Aarhus University chemist and study co-author, mentioned in a profile. “I think people would have fun playing with a frog like this using a suitable light source.”.

Each of the robot’s muscles is built using crystal elastomers. These materials are specifically manufactured to contract while they are heating, and then revert back to their original shape once cooled. In this case, Ryberg and her collaborators also added a molecule that converts near-infrared light into heat. This allows the muscles to tighten after directly exposing them to a lamp. That said, the process isn’t as simple as sticking the elastomers onto their model frog and dropping it into water.

Sources indicate that “Getting the six muscles to work together was a major challenge,” explained Brigitte Städler, a study co-author and Aarhus University chemist. “If they don’t contract in a coordinated way, the frog won’t swim forwards. It may simply spin around.”.

A lot of trial-and-error also went into concocting the elastomers themselves. In addition to contracting properly, the material needed the proper consistency to use in a 3D printer. To do this, Ryberg experimented with various molecular ingredients and molecule chain lengths to perfect the robot muscle recipe.

“In a conventional 3D printer, you typically melt a solid plastic filament. Our material is more like very thick syrup or icing that you squeeze through a piping bag when decorating a cake,” said Ryberg.

According to recent reports, the final result is a light-powered soft robot that’s quite unique, but also not in any hurry. At its best pace, the frog swam a little over three inches in about two minutes. That may not get it to its destination quickly, but the proof-of-concept successfully offers a fresh way to think about robotic design, and the ways engineers can power their creations. Until then, there is always the potential for robo-frog toys.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chainflip founder Simon Harman expressed confidence that the decentralized exchange could recover from a $12 million hack despite significant losses to liquidity providers.
  • In a recent development, the cross-chain trading platform suffered its second exploit in 10 weeks on Nov.
  • The incident also battered Chainflip's native FLIP token, which lost roughly 37% of its value after the breach, according to CoinGecko.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chainflip founder Simon Harman expressed confidence that the decentralized exchange could recover from a $12 million hack despite significant losses to liquidity providers.

In a recent development, the cross-chain trading platform suffered its second exploit in 10 weeks on Nov. 21, losing Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins from its vaults. The attack forced it to suspend deposits, withdrawals and swaps.

The incident also battered Chainflip's native FLIP token, which lost roughly 37% of its value after the breach, according to CoinGecko.

According to recent reports, in a Nov. 22 statement, Harman said he had been working with law enforcement, investigators and other stakeholders to secure the network and assess the damage.

“Although I was initially unsure about the future, I'm now relatively confident we can get back and running despite the significant losses to LPs.”.

The attacker drained 122.86 BTC from Chainflip's Bitcoin vault, alongside 520.22 ETH, approximately 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT from its Ethereum vault.

Blockchain investigators traced the Ethereum-based assets into approximately 2,909 ETH, which subsequently entered the Tornado Cash mixing protocol.

Chainflip has offered the attacker a 10% bounty to return 110.575 BTC and 2,618.1 ETH by 18:38 UTC on Nov. 23.

The company pledged to withdraw its law enforcement complaints if the funds are returned under the agreed terms.

The latest breach comes barely two months after Chainflip lost approximately $736,000 in USDT through a vulnerability affecting its Tron integration in September.

After that incident, validators approved a compensation proposal to use surplus assets held in the protocol's vaults to reimburse affected liquidity providers.

At the time, Chainflip reported approximately $1.09 million in excess USDC in its Ethereum vault and projected a network-wide surplus of about $585,000 after covering the earlier shortfall.

The November attack has now drained $3.25 million in USDC from the Ethereum vault, adding another substantial demand on the protocol's resources.

It has been revealed that september’s vote approved a way to cover the Tron shortfall. November’s BTC and ETH offer only sets the terms for a return.

After any return, the network would still have to match vault assets with balances and decide how to fund a remaining gap.

Recent findings suggest that september account-credit completion is unconfirmed. The November return terms and any later allocation or funding decision are distinct.

In a recent development, compare the approved terms of Proposal 008 with Chainflip Labs’ November offer. Solid lines mark the earlier authorization. Dashed lines mark steps conditional on a return or remaining gap.

September account-credit completion is unconfirmed. The November return terms and any later allocation or funding decision are distinct.

Harman remarked Chainflip remained a profitable business with strong distribution, but acknowledged that restoring confidence would require recovering assets and strengthening security.

He said the team was developing compensation options for affected liquidity providers, with an incident report expected on Nov. 23.

The recovery offer could replenish the vaults, but Chainflip has yet to disclose how it intends to cover outstanding liquidity-provider balances or when withdrawals will resume.

#144406. Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1200 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1200 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.
  • Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.
  • Sources indicate that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Sources indicate that surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

After Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) mentioned there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Recent findings suggest that musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a new video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

As we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement notes it “will not operate” without the $299 proposal, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

According to recent reports, so Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Recent findings suggest that brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

Recent findings suggest that the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

“It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version highlights up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself indicates is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Sources indicate that besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

According to recent reports, you can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

In a recent development, volkswagen revealed how much its fresh ID. Cross will cost, with prices starting at around $35,000 in the UK. But if you’re hoping to get the cheaper version, you’ll have to wait a bit longer.

Sources indicate that after opening orders for the ID. Cross in Europe in July, Volkswagen is preparing to launch the entry-level electric SUV in the UK.

The ID. Cross is the all-electric equivalent of the T-Cross, Volkswagen’s smallest and most affordable SUV in Europe and the UK.

Industry observers note that following the ID. Polo, the ID. Cross is the latest from Volkswagen’s electric urban family of compact cars.

According to recent reports, the electric SUV is 4,153 mm long, about the same length as the T-Cross, but its dedicated MEB+ platform offers more interior space. It seats five and offers a 475-liter boot, 20 liters more than the gas-powered T-Cross with the rear seats pushed all the way forward.

When the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

Industry observers note that like in Europe, the Volkswagen ID. Cross will be available with two battery packs in the UK: a 37 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) pack and a 52 kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) pack.

The ID. Cross with the larger 52 kWh battery offers up to 265 miles of WLTP range, while the 37 kWh version provides up to 194 miles of WLTP range.

With DC fast charging of up to 105 and 88 kW, Volkswagen said the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 80% in as little as 23 minutes.

All versions are equipped with vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, allowing it to be used as a mobile power bank for an e-bike, campsite, or other external electronic devices.

In a recent development, inside, the ID. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. Cross adopts VW’s revamped interior digital cockpit design. The setup includes a 10.25″ Digital Cockpit Pro instrument display and a 12.9″ infotainment screen. Based on driver feedback, Volkswagen brought back physical buttons for climate control and other vehicle functions.

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen will open orders for the ID. Cross Life and Style trims in the UK with the 52 kWh battery and 208 hp (211 PS) motor will go on sale on Thursday, November 19, starting at £30,260 ($40,000) and £33,675 ($44,500), respectively.

The base ID. Cross Life and Style trims with the 37 kWh battery will go on sale in January 2027, with prices starting at £26,985 ($35,500) and £30,400 ($40,100).

Industry observers note that volkswagen said the 52 kWh version is eligible for the UK government’s £1,500 ($2,000) electric car grant. Eligibility for the 37 kWh versions is expected to be confirmed soon.

According to recent reports, in Europe, Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross Trend last month, starting at €27,995 ($31,000) in Germany, including VAT.

In a recent development, as the electric counterpart to its popular T-Cross, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer stated the ID. Cross is “modern, reliable, and above all, affordable.”.

Sadly, VW has no looks to bring the ID. Cross to the US. In early 2027, it will launch the latest ID. Tiguan, which will replace the outgoing ID.4 SUV.

Tech Report: A baby turkey with a feather duster ‘mom’ has a new BFF

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (391 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it seems straight out of a Disney movie—wild animals from two different species becoming inseparable friends.
  • Last spring, the wildlife center received two likely orphaned turkey poults (young turkeys).
  • Industry observers note that “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it seems straight out of a Disney movie—wild animals from two different species becoming inseparable friends. And yet that’s what happened at the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in southeastern Pennsylvania, between a turkey and a mourning dove.

Last spring, the wildlife center received two likely orphaned turkey poults (young turkeys). To calm them down, the team put them with a feather-duster as a stand-in mother turkey. Because turkey poults are easily stressed, they are difficult to rehabilitate, according to a Facebook post by the wildlife center. In fact, one of them didn’t make it.

Industry observers note that “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote. “We paired it with a baby mourning dove of similar size, hoping they would comfort each other while eating and exploring as they are both ground eaters.”.

The pairing turned out to be a raging success. They formed an inseparable bond that Raven Ridge Wildlife Center had never seen before. Months later, the team gave the dove a soft release, meaning the bird could leave whenever it wanted. But he clearly had no intention of leaving his friend. The dove continued returning to the turkey’s cage, and the two would sit near each other on either side of the separation.

Recent findings suggest that “After a few days, we put the dove back in with the turkey, and it was clear they were happiest together,” the wildlife center explained. But “we knew keeping them caged for the rest of their lives, or keeping them just because they were cute, was neither an option nor fair to these wild animals.”.

Sources indicate that as such, the team contacted a large sanctuary in Pennsylvania to request a joint release. This way, the duo could choose whether to stick together or follow their own paths. After their soft release, the dove flew into the trees and the turkey started foraging, free to stick together or join other members of their species.

“We don’t know if they’ll stay together, but our team made sure they had a safe place until they were ready to be on their own,” the wildlife center concluded.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Bull Targets $7 – $10 After Buying Significant Below $1.

Recotr is targeting a recovery to $7 after adding to his holdings sub-$1, citing historical cycles & weak momentum readings.

It has been revealed that analyst Zach Rector claims he has nearly exhausted his buying funds after adding to positions below $1, while projecting a recovery toward $7 – $10. His argument rests on previous market cycles and a claimed record-low monthly momentum reading, not a confirmed catalyst for a rebound.

“I’m pretty much tapped out now,” Rector mentioned. He reported adding to an XRP long position at $0.88, bringing its average entry price to $1.54, and separately buying through a sponsored investment platform at about $0.93.

Zach Rector described XRP’s decline to $0.86 as a roughly 76% drawdown. He compared that with earlier bear-market losses of approximately 85% – 96%, arguing that the latest retreat could represent another accumulation period.

He cited gains of about 1,600% in the 2020–2021 cycle and 1,170% in 2024–2025. A smaller advance of roughly 700%–1,000%, he argued, could put XRP around $7–$10, depending on the starting price.

The YouTube video also cited a chart placing XRP’s monthly relative strength index at 40.53, described as its lowest reading in 14 years. That historical claim was not independently established in the transcript; a reading near 40 is also above the conventional oversold threshold of 30.

Previous rallies do not establish a floor. The analyst acknowledged that XRP could still fall toward $0.70 – $0.80 if geopolitical tensions trigger further market selling.

It has been revealed that beyond the initial recovery target, the host suggested institutional utility could eventually support prices of $20 – $30. He pointed to conversations at Ripple Swell and institutions’ interest in blockchain infrastructure, but offered no quantified link between that activity and macro demand for XRP.

Industry observers note that interest in Ripple or the XRP Ledger does not, by itself, establish that institutions will buy or hold XRP. His account of quiet institutional accumulation remained an assertion rather than documented evidence.

OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra just passed a major robot test, with a big catch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GPT-6 Astra recovered from nearly two-thirds of grasp failures when it directly controlled robots in a latest study.
  • Industry observers note that researchers from Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Bosch Research co-authored the AgentRoboCritic preprint, submitted Nov.
  • It has been revealed that the model recovered from 7,024 of the 12,163 failed actions the researchers analyzed, or 57.7%, by the end of the trials in which those failures occurred.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GPT-6 Astra recovered from nearly two-thirds of grasp failures when it directly controlled robots in a latest study. It got past roughly one in three failures to line up parts or to make a tool produce the intended effect through contact.

Industry observers note that researchers from Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Bosch Research co-authored the AgentRoboCritic preprint, submitted Nov. 19. The team collected upcoming runs on seven robot manipulation benchmarks and reanalyzed previously released GPT-6 Astra runs on five more.

It has been revealed that the model recovered from 7,024 of the 12,163 failed actions the researchers analyzed, or 57.7%, by the end of the trials in which those failures occurred. The sample came from 1,989 officially scored trials with at least one annotated failure. One benchmark, RoboDojo, supplied 9,923 of the failed actions, giving it the most weight in the pooled rate.

After a missed grab, researchers counted a recovery when a later grasp visibly lifted the object. A workaround counted too. In one trial, Astra failed to grasp a ball inside a cup, then lifted the cup with the ball still inside to prepare for a pour. Both kinds of recovery counted even if the trial ended in failure.

The recovery rate was 63.7% when a robot failed to pick up or hold an object. It was 35.7% for alignment errors and 29.6% when a tool failed to produce the intended physical change. In two benchmark settings where the model used vision alone, alignment was the most common failure. The model could move a connector or block toward an opening and still miss the position or angle it needed.

Share of each failure type that GPT-6 Astra recovered from by the end of the same trial.

Recovery cleared half of grasp failures and stayed below half for alignment and contact effects.

The rates describe failed actions in the authors’ benchmark sample. Each category has its own denominator, and a recovery could occur in a trial that ultimately failed.

In a recent development, bars use the paper’s reported percentages on a shared 0–100% scale. Counts give recovered failures over analyzed failures in each category.

The rates describe failed actions in the authors’ benchmark sample. Each category has its own denominator, and a recovery could occur in a trial that ultimately failed.

Astra used observations from the robot to issue numerical commands, such as where to position the gripper or how far to open it. In a separate study, robots ran Claude-written control programs after the coding agent had left the loop. The AgentRoboCritic researchers paired each action’s stated intent with observations before and after the move so they could judge whether it achieved what Astra meant it to do.

In a recent development, the researchers used GPT-6 Astra to label those actions and control the robots. On a separate set of 400 actions, its labels matched the initial human judgments on action outcomes about 79% of the time. For the 264 actions people marked as failures, the model agreed on the type of failure about 81% of the time.

A separate Mind2Act World preprint introduced 30 simulated manipulation tasks and found that its strongest agent struggled to maintain contact. AgentRoboCritic tracked what happened after individual moves went wrong.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin jumped more than 4% in an hour to $64,427 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday.
  • The sudden rally triggered $424 million in crypto market liquidations within an hour, according to CoinGlass, as traders betting on further declines were caught by the price reversal.
  • CoinGlass rolling one-hour snapshot supplied November 23, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin jumped more than 4% in an hour to $64,427 after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Monday.

The sudden rally triggered $424 million in crypto market liquidations within an hour, according to CoinGlass, as traders betting on further declines were caught by the price reversal.

CoinGlass rolling one-hour snapshot supplied November 23, 2026. Liquidated position values, not traders' realized net losses. Longs and shorts sum to $424.95 million; shorts account for about 88.7%. Screenshot capture time is not displayed. Later live dashboard readings can differ.

Source: CoinGlass liquidation dashboard, supplied November 23, 2026 one-hour screenshot.

Short positions accounted for $376 million, or 92.2% of the liquidations, while bullish traders lost $31.58 million.

In a recent development, bitcoin led the losses with $188 million in liquidations, 95.6% of which came from short positions. Ethereum followed with around $80 million, with shorts accounting for 92.9%.

Twelve categories with fully readable names and amounts in the supplied CoinGlass one-hour heatmap. Includes crypto assets and equity-linked perpetual markets: SOXL is distinct from XYZ:SOXL, as NVDA is from XYZ:NVDA. Other is the provider's labeled category, not a derived residual. Smaller and truncated tiles are excluded; these bars do not sum to the $424.95 million market total.

Source: CoinGlass liquidation dashboard, supplied November 23, 2026 one-hour screenshot.

Together, the two largest cryptocurrencies accounted for nearly 64% of the $403.98 million liquidated during the hour.

The concentration of short liquidations suggests that forced position closures amplified Bitcoin's initial rally, accelerating its recovery from last week's selloff.

Sources indicate that that decline had briefly pushed Bitcoin below $60,000 following Huang's abrupt departure from Nvidia on Nov. 12, which triggered turmoil across technology stocks and added pressure to an already struggling crypto market.

Monday's reversal also lifted Nvidia shares by roughly 33% to around $170 in premarket trading, reversing part of the losses accumulated during the leadership crisis.

Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang marks a dramatic reversal from its position last week, when board Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out bringing the organization's co-founder back as chief executive.

The board voted Monday unanimously to restore Huang as president, CEO, and a director after discussions that satisfied members about his candor and ability to lead the organization.

Nvidia also said senior US government officials provided input during the deliberations, giving directors confidence that Huang's return posed no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.”.

Huang's return followed mounting pressure from shareholders, technology executives and President Donald Trump, who had publicly supported reinstating the Nvidia co-founder.

Strive CEO Matt Cole welcomed the decision, saying Nvidia was the largest single holding among Strive Asset Management's clients, with nearly $100 million invested through its ETFs.

Cole stated Strive had prepared to submit a shareholder proposal requesting an advisory vote on Huang's reinstatement before Monday's market opening, but the board acted before the proposal became necessary.

Huang, who had previously expressed willingness to return, said he was honored to resume leadership of the tech giant. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will return to her previous responsibilities.

However, Huang's reinstatement does not end the investigation into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

Nvidia noted its independent board committee would complete that investigation while a newly established national security and export control committee oversees trade compliance and related risks.

The manufacturer is also recruiting a chief compliance officer and will continue cooperating with government investigations.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin's rapid recovery marks its second sharp Nvidia-linked rally within a week.

The cryptocurrency briefly reached approximately $64,600 following Nvidia's stronger-than-expected earnings last week, only to surrender most of those gains within 35 minutes.

Monday's advance returned Bitcoin to within roughly $173 of that previous high, with more than $372 million in forced short closures accompanying the move.

#144387. Industry News: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1519 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Tesla on Autopilot/FSD hit an overturned truck at 71 mph, killing 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help.
  • In a recent development, police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system.
  • Industry observers note that just before 4 a.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators notes Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.

In a recent development, police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data, and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.

Industry observers note that just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.

In a recent development, jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.

It has been revealed that then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report indicates the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.

A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson remarked the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”.

According to recent reports, so that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody said a word about Autopilot.

Industry observers note that under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.

It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and says it learned of the crash from police and the media.

Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports.

In a recent development, the report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.

It has been revealed that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.

Industry observers note that A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a massive truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.

In 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.

Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a massive, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.

In a recent development, we want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.

Sources indicate that the NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a new monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.

It has been revealed that september may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash shows how late they can be.

Our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.

It has been revealed that three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.

According to recent reports, that's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.

Compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.

Industry observers note that tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.

It has been revealed that either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes, and the crash count keeps setting records.

Recent findings suggest that we’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.
